name: Find the Error / Odd One Out
summary: Examine a set of items and identify which one is incorrect, doesn't belong, or is the odd one out.

aiGenerability.notes: AI generates sets with one intentional error. Works well for factual identification tasks. Detective/puzzle feel engages learners. Requires clear criterion for the error.

prompt.description: The question or challenge. e.g., 'Which of these is NOT a planet?' or 'One of these facts is false — which one?'

items.description: The set of options/statements to examine.

errorIndex.description: Zero-based index of the incorrect/odd item in the items array.

explanation.description: Why the identified item is wrong/odd. Explains the error or why others belong together.

criterion.description: The hidden rule or category that unites the correct items (for AI generation).

ux.mobileNotes: Keep items concise so they fit single-column layout. Use clear visual highlight on selection. Consider emoji/icons for very young learners to reduce reading load.

ageAdaptations.8-10: 3 items with obvious error. Use simple, concrete subjects (animals, colors, objects). Visual support recommended.
ageAdaptations.11-13: 4 items with subtle error. More abstract topics (facts, concepts). Error is within 1-2 details, not completely wrong.
ageAdaptations.14-16: 5 items with plausible errors. Sophisticated topics (historical events, scientific concepts). Multiple items could plausibly be wrong; learner must analyze deeply.
